strait-of-hormuz-effectively-closed-by-u.headline: Strait of Hormuz Effectively Closed by US-Iran War; Brent Above $110–$117, Global Inventories Down ~1 Billion Barrels
strait-of-hormuz-effectively-closed-by-u.summary: The US-Iran war that began February 28, 2026 has cut Hormuz throughput from 21.6 mb/d to ~10.9 mb/d by September, with OPEC+ freezing December targets for a third consecutive month on November 1 and Brent settling at $117.64 on October 30. Peace-talk optimism briefly pushed oil below $100 on November 2, but supply buffers are near exhaustion per ADNOC's CEO.
strait-of-hormuz-effectively-closed-by-u.target_indicator: Hormuz/Red Sea status → update to '2 closed'; WTI crude → ~$100/bbl; Undersea cable incidents → '0 none'
strait-of-hormuz-effectively-closed-by-u.rationale: The Strait of Hormuz is effectively shut (status = 2), representing the single largest physical supply disruption in oil-market history per CEPR/EIA/IEA data. Brent at $117.64 and WTI near $100 are directly captured by the s20 WTI indicator. The diesel/LNG transmission into industrial supply chains and the ~1bn-barrel inventory drawdown (ADNOC CEO, Nov 2) make this the highest-materiality live event in the tracker. The November 2 US-Iran peace-talk signal is a meaningful but fragile downside tail that should be monitored as a potential status shift from '2 closed' toward '1 contested'.

france-oat-bund-spread-hits-176-bp-crisi.headline: France OAT-Bund Spread Hits 176 bp — Crisis-Era Highs — as Moody's Cuts Outlook to Negative and Budget Vote Looms November 3
france-oat-bund-spread-hits-176-bp-crisi.summary: The 10-year OAT-Bund spread peaked at 176 bp on October 23 (widest since 2011), settling at 159 bp on October 30 as France's debt-to-GDP reaches 121.7% and a €43bn austerity package faces a divided parliament vote on November 3. Moody's left France at Aa3 but assigned a negative outlook on October 23; S&P review follows November 27.
france-oat-bund-spread-hits-176-bp-crisi.target_indicator: OAT-Bund 10y spread → 159 bp (peak 176 bp); Govt stability → '1 fragile'; Rating action → '1 negative outlook' (Moody's Aa3/negative, Oct 23)
france-oat-bund-spread-hits-176-bp-crisi.rationale: All three s10 indicators require simultaneous update. The spread has surpassed Italy's and Greece's (now wider-than-PIIGS), debt/GDP at 121.7% is a record, the Moody's negative outlook is a direct rating-action trigger (level 1), and the November 3 budget vote introduces binary tail risk toward level 2 (collapse/snap-election). The S&P review on November 27 is the next scheduled catalyst.

china-rare-earth-pause-legally-expires-n.headline: China Rare-Earth Pause Legally Expires November 10; US Commerce Dept Has Not Published Matching Extension Notice
china-rare-earth-pause-legally-expires-n.summary: China's suspension of its October 2025 rare-earth export-control announcements (Nos. 55–62 including the 0.1%-rule Notice 61) expires under published legal text on November 10, 2026, despite MOFCOM's informal September 28 statement referencing a wider arrangement through January 10, 2027. The US has not issued a formal matching notice, creating a legal ambiguity that could allow controls to snap back in 8 days.
china-rare-earth-pause-legally-expires-n.target_indicator: Nov-2025 pause status → update to '1 expiring' (legal text ends Nov 10; informal extension to Jan 10 not yet codified in published Chinese notice); Rare-earth export license flow → '1 slowing' (April 2025 licensing already active; exports fell 9.6% YTD Jan–Sep 2026)
china-rare-earth-pause-legally-expires-n.rationale: The gap between the published suspension-end date (Nov 10) and the informal bilateral extension (Jan 10) is uncodified on the Chinese side and unmatched by a US Federal Register notice—creating an 8-day window where controls could legally re-activate without a further formal announcement. This is precisely the s6 'pause status' indicator scenario at level 1 (expiring). April 2025 heavy-RE licensing (dysprosium, terbium) remains fully in force regardless, keeping license-flow at '1 slowing'.

ai-capex-debt-collision-drives-30-year-t.headline: AI Capex-Debt Collision Drives 30-Year Treasury to 24-Year High (5.67%, Oct 7); CCC Junk Spreads Widen 319 bp Since August
ai-capex-debt-collision-drives-30-year-t.summary: Hyperscalers (Alphabet with negative free cash flow of -$9.1bn in Q3, Meta raising capex floor to $135–145bn) are issuing 20–40-year corporate bonds en masse, competing directly with record sovereign supply and pushing the 30-year Treasury to 5.67% on October 7 (highest since 2002) and widening CCC-rated spreads by 319 bp since late August. The 10-year ACM term premium has surged to +92 bp.
ai-capex-debt-collision-drives-30-year-t.target_indicator: AI capex-vs-revenue gap concern → '2 widening fast' (Alphabet FCF negative; CCC spreads +319bp); GPU-backed debt refinancing stress → '1 signs' (CoreWeave CDS cited as early-warning; broad HY not yet confirmed); US IG OAS → elevated but not yet crisis
ai-capex-debt-collision-drives-30-year-t.rationale: The Alphabet Q3 print (negative FCF, $98.2bn total corporate debt) and Meta's capex raise represent a qualitative regime shift: hyperscalers have flipped from net cash providers to net capital consumers. The AI-debt-Treasury-yield interaction loop (more AI issuance → higher term premium → tighter financial conditions → higher AI borrowing costs) is now cited by the Fed's own market desk and LPL Research. CCC spread widening of 319 bp is a material stress signal for s8, pushing the capex-gap indicator to level 2.

boj-holds-at-1-25-oct-30-but-30-year-jgb.headline: BOJ Holds at 1.25% (Oct 30) but 30-Year JGB Hits Record 4.15–4.20%; December Hike Fully Priced; Yen Carry Unwind Risk Resurfaces
boj-holds-at-1-25-oct-30-but-30-year-jgb.summary: The Bank of Japan held its policy rate at 1.25% on October 30 as expected, but the 30-year JGB yield is at a record ~4.15–4.20% and markets are pricing a December hike to 1.50%. Seven CNBC-surveyed analysts see the 30-year JGB reaching 4%–4.1%, with BOJ normalization and shifting institutional repatriation flows compressing the rate differential — raising yen carry-trade reversal risk.
boj-holds-at-1-25-oct-30-but-30-year-jgb.target_indicator: 30-year JGB yield → ~4.15–4.20% (record high per Bloomberg/CNBC); Takaichi plan financing clarity → '1 unclear' (no credible fiscal consolidation path published); USD/JPY → monitor for yen strengthening as Dec hike approaches
boj-holds-at-1-25-oct-30-but-30-year-jgb.rationale: The 30-year JGB at a record is a direct indicator update for s2. With the BOJ at 1.25% and a December hike to 1.50% ~80% priced by CME-equivalent, the rate-differential compression accelerates carry-trade unwind risk. The simultaneous move in UK 30-year Gilts to a 28-year high and the US 30-year to 5.67% reflects a global long-bond repricing that amplifies Japan-specific fiscal risk. The Takaichi fiscal-clarity indicator remains at '1 unclear' given no published consolidation plan.

uk-30-year-gilt-at-28-year-high-gilt-bun.headline: UK 30-Year Gilt at 28-Year High; Gilt-Bund Spread Widest Since 2022 Mini-Budget Ahead of November 26 Budget
uk-30-year-gilt-at-28-year-high-gilt-bun.summary: The UK 10-year gilt-Bund spread has widened to 189 bp — the largest since the 2022 Liz Truss mini-budget crisis — with the 30-year gilt at a 28-year high and the Bank of England expected to hike to 4.0% in November. ING warns the November 26 budget could trigger significant gilt repricing if fiscal commitments are missed, with sovereign CDS up 6% to 47 bp.

proposed_indicator.label: UK gilt-Bund 10y spread (bp) & sovereign CDS stress
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = spread <120 bp and CDS <30 bp (stable); 1 = spread 120–200 bp or CDS 30–60 bp (stress, pre-budget); 2 = spread >200 bp or CDS >60 bp (crisis / LDI echo)

uk-30-year-gilt-at-28-year-high-gilt-bun.rationale: The existing s10_france story covers France/eurozone fragility but has no indicator capturing UK gilt stress specifically. The UK situation is structurally distinct: a separate sovereign, a different central bank hiking cycle, a mini-budget precedent with proven LDI/pension contagion (2022), and a November 26 fiscal event with binary tail risk. The gilt-Bund spread at 189 bp — the widest since that crisis — and sovereign CDS jumping 6% are not captured by any existing tracker indicator. Given the 2022 UK LDI blow-up's systemic implications (s14_pensions crossover), this gap warrants a new composite indicator within s10 rather than a new story.

boj-officials-signal-rate-hikes-every-fe.headline: BOJ officials signal rate hikes every few months; 30yr JGB yields at 3.88%, 10yr at 2.61% — carry trade unwind risk acute
boj-officials-signal-rate-hikes-every-fe.summary: The 10-year JGB yield dropped to 2.755% on October 23 (below MUFG's Q4 forecast floor of 2.85%) as Takaichi's explicit rejection of Abenomics-style reflation calmed near-term BoJ-behind-the-curve fears, yet the 30-year JGB yield remains near 3.93% (auction Oct 8: 4.109%), reflecting a persistent long-end fiscal risk premium as the FY2027 budget — the Takaichi administration's first full cycle — remains unfunded.
boj-officials-signal-rate-hikes-every-fe.rationale: Both named JGB indicators in s2_japan are updated: the 30-year yield remains elevated at ~3.93% (auction cleared at 4.109%), confirming the long-end fiscal premium persists. The 10-year's drop below 2.8% — while calming near-term carry-trade risk — reflects flight-to-haven demand from global risk aversion (AI selloff, Middle East) rather than fiscal improvement, keeping the 'Takaichi plan financing clarity' sub-indicator at 1 (unclear): the FY2027 budget has no deficit-bond solution yet. Net assessment: short-end calm, long-end stress intact.

synchronized-global-sovereign-bond-rout-.headline: Synchronized global sovereign bond rout: US 10y at 4.80%, UK 30y at 5.82% (highest since 1998), German 10y at 2011 highs
synchronized-global-sovereign-bond-rout-.summary: The 10-year OAT/Bund spread hit 174.6 bps on Oct 22 (171.8 bps on Oct 23), with French 10-year yields at 5.05%, after the National Assembly finance committee rejected the 2027 budget revenue package 31-to-3, injecting acute political risk ahead of the April 2027 presidential election. Early contagion signals are visible in Italian and Spanish spreads, and Moody's already holds France at Aa3 with a negative outlook.
synchronized-global-sovereign-bond-rout-.rationale: The OAT-Bund spread at 171.8 bps — now wider than Italy and Greece — is a direct, named indicator in s10_france. The budget's parliamentary collapse (finance committee 31-3 rejection) also escalates the 'Govt stability' sub-indicator from 1 (fragile) toward 2 (collapse-or-snap-election risk), and Moody's negative outlook keeps the 'Rating action' sub-indicator at 1 with downgrade risk rising. This is the most acute near-term eurozone financial-stability signal of the week.

coreweave-bond-yields-hit-16-stock-40-in.headline: CoreWeave bond yields hit ~16%, stock -40% in October: GPU-backed debt refinancing stress turns acute across neocloud sector
coreweave-bond-yields-hit-16-stock-40-in.summary: CoreWeave's ~$50–52 billion debt load triggered a simultaneous stock and bond selloff — bonds implying 15–16% yields, CDS spreads above 11%, stock down ~40% in October — spreading to Oracle and dragging the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down >13% in October. Elon Musk warned debt markets have 'almost entirely shut off access' for AI data-center companies without independent revenue, signaling sector-wide refinancing stress rather than a single-name event.
coreweave-bond-yields-hit-16-stock-40-in.target_indicator: GPU-backed debt refinancing stress (0 none / 1 signs / 2 acute)
coreweave-bond-yields-hit-16-stock-40-in.rationale: CoreWeave's bond yields at 15–16% and CDS spreads >11%, combined with Musk's statement that debt markets have shut off for neocloud firms, directly activates the 'GPU-backed debt refinancing stress' indicator from 1 (signs) to 2 (acute). The AI capex-vs-revenue gap indicator also widens (CoreWeave guiding $35–39B capex vs ~$13B revenue). The Philadelphia Semis -13% in October further registers in AI-circular-financing systemic risk. This is the clearest single new data point for s8 this week.

houthi-attacks-push-brent-to-117-6-month.headline: Houthi attacks push Brent to $117 (6-month high); Iran accelerates Hormuz surveillance with new naval units; October flows volatile and below pre-war average
houthi-attacks-push-brent-to-117-6-month.summary: Brent crude briefly topped $117/bbl on Oct 23 after Yemen's Houthis launched fresh attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities and the port of Yanbu, while Iran deployed new military units to expand surveillance of the Strait of Hormuz. Although some daily crude readings near prewar levels, October-to-date Middle East exports remain below pre-war averages, ~40% of oil is bypassing Hormuz via alternatives, and Saudi Aramco's CEO warned inventory rebuilding could take up to two years.
houthi-attacks-push-brent-to-117-6-month.rationale: Fresh Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and Iranian Hormuz surveillance escalation directly update s20_sea_lanes. WTI/Brent at ~$113–117 is a live indicator reading. The Hormuz/Red Sea status indicator should remain at 1 (contested) given that flows are partial and volatile with convoy rerouting. This also has cascading effects on s5_china_deflation (cost-push via energy), s18_food_fertilizer (fertilizer input disruption via Hormuz), and s4_dev_debt (energy-import stress on frontier economies), but the primary home is s20.
